subject: Genetics
title: The Access Problem
description: A quick, practical guide to The Access Problem.

hook.text: Zolgensma: $2.1 million. Casgevy: $2.2 million per patient. Most of the world's patients will never afford it.

buildup.text: Gene therapies are one-time treatments replacing lifetimes of care. Companies say long-term savings justify the price.

discovery.text: Sickle cell is most common in sub-Saharan Africa—where Casgevy's price equals decades of national per-capita income.

twist.text: Some nations negotiate pay-for-results deals: pay only if the therapy works after years. New models are emerging.

climax.text: Without solving access, gene therapy stays a miracle for the rich. The science works. The economics don't—yet.

punchline.text: The cure exists. The price decides who gets it.

quiz.question: Why is gene therapy access a global problem?
options: Costs are too high for most health systems
